overall: Informal resolution finding the Board violated the OML by omitting the specific executive session purpose from the November 14, 2011 notice and from its open-session announcement and minutes; the Board was ordered to comply and amend the minutes, and an out-of-scope litigation-discussion claim was declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board held a November 14, 2011 executive session without listing it in the meeting notice.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to include the specific executive session purpose in the notice for its November 14, 2011 executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the open session minutes did not state the specific executive session topic; the Board also did not publicly state all executive session purposes before entering.
allegations.key_passage: The Board also failed to publicly state prior to the executive session, and failed to include in the open session minutes, all of the executive sessions purposes that the Board relied upon.

allegations.summary: Complainant argued the discussion at the November 14, 2011 executive session was not a proper executive session purpose; raised outside the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review this allegation, as it was not raised in the original complaint filed with the Board.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
Amend the minutes of the November 14, 2011 open meeting to reflect all executive session purposes relied upon and topics discussed, within thirty days of receipt of the letter.
remedy_passage: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law. Additionally, we order the Board to amend the minutes of its November 14, 2011 open meeting to reflect all executive session purposes relied upon, and topics discussed by the Board during that meeting.
